In January of this year my girlfriend and I moved in together and I had always been pretty financially fine, but I spent my money on stupid things. When we moved in together we set up a budget and started to get a nice emergency fund started.

A month or so later I go to switch all my car registration and such to the new state and they won't pass my car because my wheel bearings are bad and my tie rods need replaced. We only have this one car between us so I have no option but to get it fixed. Emergency fund was depleted at that point.

Fast forward two months we're getting our finances straightened out again and then I end up needing to go to the ER for severe abdomen pains and it is diverticulitis and the doctor tells me I can't work for a week. Between that and my current job not getting any business and me still being part time status they start cutting hours and it is making bills harder to keep up with.

Two months more and diverticulitis strikes again and this time a bit worse. They keep me in the hospital for two days and tell me I can't work again for another week. Our emergency fund is gone by this point and I'm starting to stress a bit.

About a week and a half ago I'm feeling good and working and my girlfriend got a new slightly higher paying position where she works so things seem to be going well. I'm at work on a Thursday night(3rd shift job) and I'm getting terrible pains in my side. I think damn it can't be diverticulitis again already. This time the pain was in my right side and not my left and it was getting worse fast. Work sends me to the hospital to get checked out and I end up having to get my appendix out.

Doctor tells me I can't work until after my check up appointment which is in two weeks but for a manufacturing job they usually make you wait four weeks to return to work.

At this point I'm at a loss. I have no idea what to do. I'm trying to keep my composure around my girlfriend and her kid but it is hard. This is the first time I've ever really been in any sort of real financial trouble. I just turned 26 yesterday so I am no longer covered under my parents insurance. I am starting college this fall with my GI Bill and getting insurance through them but I'm scared of ending up having to go back to the doctor for something before my new insurance kicks in. They suggested I get a colonoscopy and meet up with general surgeon to possibly get part of my intestine removed, but until I get the insurance I can't make any appointments for those.

Sorry for the long story but I just wanted to give a background of what I'm faced with for the advice I'm seeking. I'm just curious if there is anything out there I can do to help with my situation. I am unable to get temporary unemployment because I'm technically not allowed to work right now. I don't really have any family I can ask to borrow any money from. I know that most ways to make money online are scams but I'm curious if any of you know any legitimate ones. Do I have any other options for any sort of assistance?

Again I'm sorry for the long post and to burden anyone who reads this with my troubles but I'm not sure what else to do. Thanks for your time. I'll be away from my phone for an hour or so before I can check for replies but I will as soon as I can.

You mention "ways to make money online". This, effectively, involves either the buying and selling of drugs, or malware spreading and scamming, both most likely using bitcoins. I wouldn't suggest anything like this, since you could just end up going down a rabbit hole, with things getting worse and worse if you are caught. Also the amount of time and computer-knowledge required is steep for the average human.

You could consider getting a short loan from the bank, and then when you get better in 2-3 weeks, you and your SO can work and really scrounge to pay back any debts you already have. You could consider meeting with your bank and discussing some possible solutions.

I would obviously recommend first taking subtle actions to reduce expenditure temporarily. I know this will feel terrible, and having to break it to your SO could be really tough, but trust me, these kind of problems will only get worse if you brush them under the rug and what not. Areas include reducing use of motorised transport and hence petrol, reduce eating out, increase consumption of cheaper foods, i.e. rice and potatoes, and for example skipping on that serlion steak you have once or twice a week, and instead go for chicken breast or something.

Overall this is a small problem, try not to blow it too much out of proportion. This is a problem caused by a most likely a short term cause, and isn't because of some chronic issue with your financials.

EDIT: And to be honest, if you're lucky someone here will help you. It happens quite a lot that someone incredibly thoughtful will donate to, for example, your paypal. Or atleast, they will donate, and wish for you to pay back later.
